title: Every Love Story is a Tragedy (A Berserk Essay)
summary: Valentine's essay arguing Berserk's Golden Age arc is fundamentally a love story between Guts and Casca, and that every love story is a tragedy. Drawing on Nietzsche, Aristotle and Greek tragedy, NH argues love requires vulnerability, responsibility and the suicide of reason, that fear of love is life denial, and that Griffith's betrayal is cowardly renunciation of humanity.
claims: The ultimate purpose of life is love
Berserk is a love story: the battles supplement the Guts and Casca romance
Love is the strongest human passion and what motivates people to work and to go to war
Tragedy's catharsis forces you to face that similar catastrophe will happen in your own life
Berserk fans tend to be emotionally sensitive people, not gore addicts
Trauma makes people build walls that keep pain out but also keep love and joy out
Love is first and foremost responsibility, a restriction you impose on yourself, not freedom
Berserk is one of the finest feminist works, showing the hell a world without protection creates for women
True love only blossoms when both people remove their masks and show weaknesses
Falling in love is irrational; on a risk-reward calculation nobody would do it
Many young men now refuse marriage or love out of fear; that is really fear of vulnerability and distrust of their own judgement
The joy of the right partner outweighs the pain of betrayal
NH is married, trusts his wife more than himself and gives her the keys to everything he owns
Love is letting go, not clinging; it is the suicide of reason
Griffith does not love because reason always overrides his emotions, a self-inflicted sociopathy that leads to his downfall
Judeau shows quiet desperation: never expressing love out of fear made him miserable
It is better to suffer at the end of love than never to love; fear of love is life denial
Love is an equal exchange that makes you grow; adoration is one-sided and transactional
Guts left the Hawks because of low self-worth, not believing he deserved love
Love exists beyond good and evil; it is the choices made because of it that are good or evil
Love is war, the best battle you'll fight; perfect frictionless romances are unrealistic
Only his wife can really hurt him with words because she knows all his weaknesses
Griffith's betrayal makes him human and a coward, not an Übermensch; Apostles are all cowards who refused to suffer
Being an Übermensch means embracing suffering and humanity fully, not rejecting emotions
Love is always worth it, even in the face of absolute misfortune
